**Short answer:**  
No – you should never use someone else’s Stripe secret key, even just for testing.

**Why it’s risky**

| Reason | What could happen |
|--------|------------------|
| **Secret key exposure** | The key lets anyone spend money or read all of that Stripe account’s data.|
| **Billing** | If the key is used, it will charge the *friend’s* Stripe account and you’ll be billed on their card.|
| **Legal & privacy** | Using a key that doesn’t belong to you can violate Stripe’s terms of service and potentially privacy laws.|
| **Audit trail** | It’s hard to trace activity back to you if you’re not the account owner. |

**Safe way to test payments**

| Step | What to do |
|------|------------|
| 1. **Create your own Stripe account** | Sign up on Stripe’s [free tier](https://stripe.com) – it costs nothing to start. |
| 2. **Use test mode** | In your new account, all API keys are “test” keys. You can run live‑look‑alike transactions without any money changing hands. |
| 3. **Generate a test secret key** | In the Dashboard → Developers → API keys → New key. This will be the key your app should use during development. |
| 4. **Set the key in your environment** | Store it in a `.env` file or your platform’s secrets manager; never hard‑code it in public code. |
| 5. **Switch to live mode only when you’re ready to accept real payments** | When you’re ready to launch, replace the test key with your live secret key in the same secure spot. |

**If you still need a quick “demo” key**

* Stripe provides a *“Issuing” test key* that you can copy; it’s not linked to any real account.  
* Or use the official [Stripe “test cards”](https://stripe.com/docs/testing#cards) – you don’t need a real key at all, just the test mode.

**Bottom line**  
Create and use your own Stripe keys. That keeps your finances, your friend’s finances, and your app’s security all clean and compliant.
